answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The grove multiplier is published, charged in comet, and ripple lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4188 identities would post 3025 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
